evidence.claim: Craft already defines ledger.yml as source of truth and index.json as rebuildable derived data.
Craft already expects stable row IDs and machine indexes for common access patterns.
The schema states YAML owns fields and validation rules, while generated indexes are not source authority.
The current index contract already names required ledger indexes and .craft/index.json.
Typed items contain nested and conditional fields that CSV import must preserve carefully.
Current examples embed positional index pointers, which can drift after row reordering and are better treated as generated compatibility data.
Live examples include row families beyond the initial schema contract, so projection generation must define or flag them.
Prior Craft refine work kept public/private boundary and generated runtime refresh as explicit gates.

non_evidence: Private workspace ledgers and unpublished product state were not copied into this public Craft run.
